newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar barely up, new contract highs hit.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar barely up, new contract highs hit.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures surged to life of contract highs across the board in early dealings before easing slightly by midsession.

At 1133 EDT, July stood 0.01 cent firmer at 11.49 cents per lb, having traded from a contract high of 11.58 to a low of 11.34 cents. October also climbed to a new high of 11.34 cents before easing to 11.29, unchanged from the previous close.
The back months stood 0.07 higher to 0.04 cent lower.
Despite the pullback from the highs and a technically overbought market, analysts expect the speculators to continue to add to long positions as prices rise amid increasing liquidity, analysts said.
Open interest in July rose 2,665 lots as of early Tuesday, to 77,212 lots.
"It's off to the races again," a trader said. "New highs will continue to attract new buying."
Dealers said the market could stage a pullback until the July contract draws closer to its expiry, on June 30.
Resistance was seen at each point higher, traders said, citing steady producer selling.
"All this is new ground so when you talk about resistance it's right here," a trader said.
Other analysts cited July chart resistance at 11.65-11.70, a high from late April. Support was seen from 11.20 to 11.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 19,231 lots as of 1100 EDT.
